results.text_excerpt: What to pack for India depends far more on season and region than most generic checklists let on — a desert winter in Rajasthan, a monsoon month in Kerala and a beach week in Goa call for genuinely different bags, not the same fifteen items reshuffled. The constants across all of them are modest, breathable layers, comfortable closed shoes, and a few small items that solve problems generic advice tends to skip. Everything below is organised by what actually changes trip to trip, not a single one-size list. The constants, regardless of season or region A few things belong in every India packing list no matter where or when you're going: lightweight, breathable fabrics (cotton and linen outperform synthetics in the heat and humidity); modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees for temples, mosques and most heritage sites; comfortable closed-toe walking shoes for fort and old-city cobblestones; a lightweight scarf or shawl, useful for modesty, sun protection and cold air-conditioning

The key to dealing with temperature variation is layering.  Layering is one of the five principles of light travel .  The layers trap air (and therefore heat) against the body.  Multiple thin layers are actually warmer than one thick layer. Add on a waterproof outer layer, and you are almost guaranteed warmth.
